2. Heard Sri Jagdish Prasad Mishra, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Sunil Kumar Dwivedi,
Advocate holding brief of Sri Prashant Ji Pandey, learned counsel for the informant as well as Sri Jai Kishan Chaurasia, learned State Law Officer for the State and perused the record.
3. Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No.93 of 2024, under Sections 323, 354-B, 376 I.P.C., Police Station- Kairana, District- Shamli, during the pendency of trial.
Deepak vs State Of U.P. on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129352979/
1

PROSECUTION STORY:
4. The applicant is stated to have outraged the modesty of the victim on 28.2.2024 at about 04:30 p.m. and had assaulted her causing injuries to her.

ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF APPLICANT:
5. The applicant is absolutely innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
6. The FIR is delayed by about half a day and there is no explanation of the said delay caused.
7. The injuries sustained by the victim are simple in nature.
The case of property dispute between the parties has been converted to that of sexual assault by the informant.

8. There is no allegation of rape in the FIR or in the statement of the victim recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C., subsequently at the stage of recording the statement of the victim under Section 164 Cr.P.C., the allegations of rape have been made after legal consultation.

9. There is no sign of struggle between the two at the time of commissioning of rape as is but evident from the examination-in-chief of the victim, who has been examined as PW-2.
10.
Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
11. The criminal history of two cases assigned to the applicant stands explained in paragraph-17 of the affidavit filed with bail application.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 6.3.2024 and is ready to cooperate with trial.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.
ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF STATE/OPPOSITE PARTY 12.
The bail application has been opposed but the submissions raised by the learned counsel for the applicant could not be disputed.

CONCLUSION:
13.

The Supreme Court in Prabhakar Tewari Vs. State of U.P. and another, 2020 (11) SCC 648 has observed that pendency of several criminal cases against an accused itself cannot be a basis for refusal of bail, if otherwise his case of bail is made out.

entities.text: Prabhakar Tewari Vs. State of U.P. and another, 2020 (11) SCC 648
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 14. The well-known principle of "Presumption of Innocence Unless Proven Guilty," gives rise to the concept of bail as a rule and imprisonment as an exception.

Deepak vs State Of U.P. on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129352979/
2

15. A person's right to life and liberty, guaranteed by Article 21 of the Indian Constitution, cannot be taken away simply because the person is accused of committing an offence until the guilt is established beyond a reasonable doubt.

Article 21 of the Indian Constitution states that no one's life or personal liberty may be taken away unless the procedure established by law is followed, and the procedure must be just and reasonable.

The said principle has been recapitulated by the Supreme Court in Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690.
16.

entities.text: Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Reiterating the aforesaid view the Supreme Court in the case of Manish Sisodia Vs. Directorate of Enforcement 2024 INSC 595 has again emphasised that the very well-settled principle of law that bail is not to be withheld as a punishment is not to be forgotten.

entities.text: Manish Sisodia Vs. Directorate of Enforcement 2024 INSC 595
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is high time that the Courts should recognize the principle that ?bail is a rule and jail is an exception?.
17. Learned State Law Officer could not bring forth any exceptional circumstances which would warrant denial of bail to the applicant.
18. It is settled principle of law that the object of bail is to secure the attendance of the accused at the trial.

No material particulars or circumstances suggestive of the applicant fleeing from justice or thwarting the course of justice or creating other troubles in the shape of repeating offences or intimidating witnesses and the like have been shown by learned State Law Officer.

19. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record, and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case,
the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

20. Let the applicant- Deepak involved in aforementioned case crime number be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with evidence.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the Trial Court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
21. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
Identity, status and residence proof of the applicant and sureties be verified by the court concerned before the bonds are accepted.

22. It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the Deepak vs State Of U.P. on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129352979/
